Use N–mm–MPa units and Euler–Bernoulli beam theory (small deflection, linear elastic).
Analyze a cantilever beam of length L = 1800 mm, fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L.
The beam is made of structural steel with E = 200000 MPa and constant second moment of area I = 1200000 mm^4.
A downward point load P = 2000 N is applied at the free end.
The bending moment is M(x) = P·(L − x), which is zero at the free end.
The standard physically correct cantilever solution applies; the previously mentioned "zero free-end rotation" and "constant moment P·L" assumptions are discarded entirely.
Determine the slope at the free end as θ = P·L² / (2·E·I).
Determine the vertical deflection at the free end as δ = P·L³ / (3·E·I).
Report the slope in radians and optionally in degrees.
Report the deflection in mm, downward (negative if the vertical axis points upward).
The expected results are θ = 0.0135 rad (≈ 0.7735°) and δ = 16.2 mm downward.
